node.title: Common-factor product-cover exclusion
node.closure: common two-by-three factor-product covers are incompatible with an unsafe rank-eleven survivor
node.statement: At the official KoalaBear rank-eleven rich-container terminal, let U_i be every nontransverse represented row space and W_i its promoted container. If fixed polynomial subspaces P,B have dim(P)<=2 and dim(B)<=3 and every U_i<=W_i<=g_iB for some nonzero g_i in P, then sum_i U_i lies in span(PB), of dimension at most six. The proved low-span payment forces dimension at least seven on every unsafe survivor, so this complete common-factor product-cover branch is paid. Under the stronger hypotheses W_i=g_iB with b projectively distinct pencil members and selected zero sets of size H in a universe of size at most m, the fixed locus Z(B) union Z(P) has size at least ceil((bH-m)/(b-1)); for b=8406, H=42452, m=1116048 this is 42325. This product-cover subclass is not identified with the general upstream base-field-normalized split-pencil census.
